gates.text: Read the complete [Statechart guide](artifacts.md#statechart) before ordinary agent exec. This is skill-guided artifact work, not a Gateway tool or native controller. Inspect the spec, config and executable view first; use owned scratch outside the repository and preserve native permissions and untrusted-code isolation. Doctor installs nothing; necessary trusted toolchain setup uses the guide's explicit verified path, never upstream scripts or automatic mise.

1. Turn every reader-agreed rule into an INVARIANT, adding model variables when needed. Never weaken a rule to obtain a pass. Write Next as named actions. Give intentional terminal states a labeled stuttering action; an unmodeled exit is a real NoDeadlock (or CHECK_DEADLOCK name-collision) finding, not a reason to disable checking.

2. Use the reader's state and event words, not variable or code names. A pure state(vars) returns a string, hierarchy array or parallel-region object; step(action,from,to), group(vars), colors and title customize presentation. State/group run at most once per model state and step once per transition; chart and report share those answers. TLA sequences have 1-based object keys and sets are arrays. Explain hidden deciding values in event labels, but do not replace automatic cross-region conditions with misleading brackets.

3. Aim for about twenty arrows without hiding bugs. Split a label when a same-label step matters. Preserve every bug-path state and mark; never merge states breaking different rules or turn a definite break into a hidden mayBreak. If hiding steps, keep each state reachable from a start, retain an exit wherever the model has one, hide every model step of an arrow or none, and disclose the hidden steps.

4. Read the report, not only the picture. breaks means all represented states break the named rule; mayBreak means only some do. Explain each state's rules from the Legend, including parallel-region combination marks. TLC explores beyond bugs. Bound constants/constraints and disclose VIEW/SYMMETRY representative-state edges. Rules beyond CONSTRAINT/ACTION_CONSTRAINT can still fail and shortest bug paths are retained, but unexplored boundary states have no deadlock verdict. Do not claim excluded steps or omitted states were explored.

5. TLC checks the original config with one worker, then removes discovered broken rules and rechecks. Later checks stop at 100,000 distinct states; timeout/error/budget leaves Rules not checked, never a pass. A bounded property's counterexample may differ because variable order changes. tlc.out preserves original-config output; tlc-RULE.out carries later discoveries. Report the native exit status and any incomplete rule verification separately from drawing success.

6. The 500-state chart budget does not limit the original proof. Above it, draw only broken-rule paths; if no rule breaks, no chart.mmd is produced. Reduce the model to show a full graph, not to hide a failure. Present Mermaid text and, when an image is needed, use the guide's pinned Pele renderer. Preserve breaks/mayBreak/bugPath/repeats marks and readable light/dark colors. A render error returns the Mermaid and actual error; do not silently switch renderers.

7. Hand the reader the chart, numbered shortest paths, each broken rule in plain words, omitted behavior and a rerun command with a new output directory. Replay each code-model bug path against real code, one action per step, before calling it a product bug. A failed replay challenges the model first. A passing chart explains behavior within checked bounds, not an unlimited guarantee. Remove consumed owned scratch, never another owner's files.

**Reply.** Chart/Mermaid, checked rules and bounds, broken-rule paths with real-code replay evidence or named missing proof, exclusions, rerun command and actual rendering errors. No automatic repair, publication or live-service mutation.
